claude.performance_metric: divested 51% stake ~9.3 years post-close at ~$8.75bn valuation vs ~$16.7bn paid (roughly half)
claude.rationale: Section 2 documents a whole-entity statutory merger in which T4 (FPGA/PLD product families and customers) and T5 (design/development operations, leveraging Intel manufacturing) transferred together, and T6 (people) transferred and were operated as a business unit — so no product-vs-process (gap_45=0) or process-vs-organization (gap_56=0) structural mismatch at closing. Section 4 states P4 product-process disruption was "not documented as a discrete tier-transfer fracture" and P5 process-organization fracture was "None documented," so both pathways are coded 0. The only concretely documented adverse outcome (section 3-4) is the valuation decline realized at divestiture, with no primary source attributing a specific tier-interface fracture.

gemini.performance_metric: divested 51% majority stake after ~9.3 years at ~$8.75bn valuation (vs ~$16.7bn paid)
gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-entity statutory merger where Altera's products, processes, and organization transferred together into Intel, so there were no structural gaps at closing (gap_45=0, gap_56=0). While the business was eventually spun out and sold at a lower valuation, the dossier does not document specific product-process (p4) or process-organization (p5) integration fractures.

grok.performance_metric: sold 51% stake ~112 months post-close at ~52% of original value
grok.rationale: gap_45=0 and gap_56=0 because section 2 states T4, T5 and T6 all transferred whole (FPGA products, design operations and people moved together into Intel PSG). p4_pathway=0 because section 4 explicitly states 'Not documented as a discrete tier-transfer fracture' for T4-T5; p5_pathway=0 because section 4 states 'None documented' for T5-T6.
